item: the first-duck ramp from the pause frame (04 "(measure) captures" 4)

candidates.description: offlineDuck as ported: on an empty timeline cancelAndHoldAtTime does nothing and the first exponential ramp inserts setValueAtTime(1, pause), so the fall starts at the pause frame (duck-first-ramp: frame 19968, t = 0.75 s); later ducks fall from the previous event; a cancel inside a ramp holds the float ExponentialRampAtTime value, cached lazily
the fall starts at t: a setValueAtTime(held, t) before the first duck's ramps (what offlineDuck would do if an event already existed)

not a rule candidate: ExponentialRampAtTime with the double quotient f64(v2) / f64(v1) instead of the float v2 / v1; the cases see it far below their -140 dB threshold, so the float quotient is pinned by the param.rs unit tests, not by the refs

outcome: candidate 0 nulls every case bit for bit; the rule is kept (the fall starts at the pause frame via the inserted setValueAtTime(1, pause)). (b) and (c) were not needed
caseNotes: duck-call-order: the 04 sketch (a later-called hap with an earlier t in the same pause) cannot come from a job: planEngineJob orders haps by onset (selectHaps, ties in query order). The case pins call order with two ducks at the same t (the second call cancels the first's ramps); duck_in_job_order_not_time_order pins the unsorted order on a hand-made job

duck-multi-target: a target orbit no hap uses cannot be in a micro case: superdough logs 'duck target orbit 7 does not exist' through its error logger and the render page reports it as an 'other' render error, which the engine (decision 14, a silent no-op) does not. The case ducks two existing orbits (arrays, and a scalar duckattack that falls back to attackArr[0]); duck_missing_target_noop pins the no-op
